# Energy skill: capacity, load, infusion

Every online struct draws power continuously, and **load > capacity = offline = you cannot act**. Energy is therefore the substrate of everything: no power, no mining, no building, no defense. This skill is "I need power / I'm offline / how do I budget power" — raising your own capacity (infusion), distributing it (substations/allocations), and recovering from overload. *Earning* from energy (running providers, selling, the flywheel) lives in [`structs-commerce`](/skills/structs-commerce/SKILL.html).

Conventions (TX_FLAGS, `--` rule, charge bar, one-tx-at-a-time) are in [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html). **Interface:** if Structs Desktop MCP is connected, use `structs_intel` for power/economy reads. Reactor infusion lifecycle controls are currently **Team Ops → Industry → Production Tauri/web-board handlers**, not a `structs_action` action or a new MCP tool; use the human board or the `structsd` fallback below. See [interface routing](/skills/conventions.html#choosing-your-interface-capability-aware).

> **Denomination footgun**: infusion amounts must carry the `ualpha` suffix — `60000000ualpha`, not `60000000`. Missing denom = failed tx. Generator infusions accept exactly **one** coin; a comma-separated list is rejected.

> **Spend-source footgun**: reactor and generator infusions are paid from your **player vault** by default, not from your signing key. Alpha on the key does not count unless you pass `--delegator-address [your-address]` (reactors only). See [conventions — vault](/skills/conventions.html#your-alpha-lives-in-your-vault).

## When to use it

- A struct won't go online, or you went offline (load exceeded capacity).
- You're about to build and need to confirm power headroom.
- You want more capacity (you have Alpha to infuse).
- You're setting up substations/allocations to distribute power.

## Decisions

### "I need more capacity" decision tree

```
Have Alpha Matter?
├── Yes → Infuse a reactor   → safest, immediate, reversible (cooldown), 1g ≈ 1 kW − commission   [default]
│         or Infuse a generator → 2-10 kW/g but IRREVERSIBLE and raidable (only with defense in place)
└── No  → Buy capacity via an agreement from a provider → ongoing cost; see structs-commerce
```

**Beginner default**: infuse your **guild's reactor**. Capacity rises automatically — no substation wiring needed for your own use. Pick the lowest commission you can.

> **Infusing a reactor powers *you*, not the guild substation.** Infusion adds ~96% (at 4% commission) to **your own** `capacity` and the commission to the reactor — it does **not** raise any substation's capacity or other members' `capacitySecondary`. To feed the shared guild pool, someone must route capacity in with an **allocation** (below). See [energy.md — infusion](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/energy#creating-capacity-infusion-splits-964).

### Spreading stake pays: the diversity bonus

Base reactor power is a flat **1:1** on fuel before commission. On top of that the chain pays an **owner diversity bonus** on your post-commission reactor power, based on how evenly your stake is spread across *eligible* (bonded, unjailed) reactors. Effective reactor count is `(Σ power)² / Σ power²`; the bonus is `50% × min(1, (effective − 1) / 9)`:

| Eligible reactors, equal split | Bonus |
|---|---|
| 1 | 0% |
| 2 | ≈ 5.56% |
| 3 | ≈ 11.11% |
| 5 | ≈ 22.22% |
| 10+ | 50% |

Unequal holdings earn less; dust spread across reactors earns almost nothing. Generators and received allocations do not count, and a guild's portfolio is separate from its members'. Read yours with `structsd query structs owner-reactor-diversity [owner-id]` — use the returned `usableBonus`/`storedCapacity`, not your own arithmetic, because the chain floors once in integer math.

> **Adding stake to a reactor you already dominate can *lower* your total power**, because it shrinks the effective count faster than the new base power grows. Preview the portfolio before signing a large infusion into your biggest reactor. A capacity drop triggers the ordinary brownout cascade. "Infuse more into the same reactor" is not always the fix for low power.

### Stake cap: a reactor can refuse you

Once ten validators are bonded the **reactor stake cap** activates (and stays active): any inflow — `reactor-infuse`, `staking delegate`, migration in, cancelling a defusion — that would leave the validator above **30%** of bonded stake is rejected with `reactor stake cap exceeded` (code 1613). Check before you send: `structsd query structs reactor-stake-share [reactor-id]` returns `capActive`, `capBps`, `externalDepositHeadroom` (room for new Alpha) and `bondedRedelegationHeadroom` (room for a migration from another bonded reactor). Empty headroom strings mean the cap is inactive, not that the reactor is full. Existing above-cap positions are not evicted; they just cannot grow.

**Reactor vs generator**: reactor is the safe default (reversible via a defusion cooldown, not raidable). Generators give far more kW per gram but the Alpha is **annihilated** (no defusion) and a raided generator takes the infused matter with it — only infuse generators you can defend (they're armoured with higher HP, but still a target). Decisions live in [`playbooks/situations/resource-rich`](https://structs.ai/playbooks/situations/resource-rich).

### "Am I about to go offline?"

Online requires load to fit the chain's usable capacity. Player passive draw is 25,000 mW; each online struct adds its `passiveDraw`. `scripts/power-budget.sh [player-id] --type [struct-type-id]` reports an exact stored margin and the proposed passive draw at one query height. It does not prove live reactor eligibility, supply validity or that activation will succeed. Confirm the actual action with native preflight and its committed result. If you're already offline, use the recovery procedure below.

## Power math

```
storedMargin = (capacity + capacitySecondary) - (load + structsLoad)
```

- `capacity` — your own generation (infusions); the only part you can allocate out.
- `capacitySecondary` — received from a substation you're connected to.
- `load` — power you've allocated to others.
- `structsLoad` — player passive (25,000 mW) + sum of `passiveDraw` of your online structs.

Units are milliwatts (1 W = 1,000 mW; 1 ualpha = 1 mW).

The chain checks usable primary capacity and the connected substation when deciding
whether the player is online. Stored values can lag bounded repairs. A positive
`storedMargin` is a diagnostic, not authorization to add load. The helper refuses
failed or incomplete reads; a failed substation query never means zero capacity.

### Worked load budget

Command Ship (50,000 mW) + Ore Extractor (500,000) + Ore Refinery (500,000) + player passive (25,000) = **1,075,000 mW** of `structsLoad`. To keep all online you need `capacity + capacitySecondary ≥ 1,075,000`. Infusing ~1,120,000 ualpha into a 4%-commission reactor nets ~1,075,000 mW to you — just enough; leave a margin.

## Procedure — raise your own capacity (reactor infusion)

1. Check capacity and vault Alpha: `structsd query structs player [id]` (`playerInventory.rocks` is the vault's spendable ualpha). If the Alpha is on your signing key instead, either move it (`structsd tx bank send [key] [vault-address] [amount]ualpha`) or plan to pass `--delegator-address`.
2. Pick a reactor and read its commission and **validator address**: `structsd query structs reactor [id]` (the `validator` field, `structsvaloper1...` — the command takes the validator address, not the reactor ID). Then `structsd query structs reactor-stake-share [id]` for cap headroom. A jailed or unbonded validator produces **zero** usable energy from infusions until it is bonded again; `reactor-restart` queues the resync afterwards.
3. Infuse (CLI prompts — review validator, commission, amount, and spend source):
   ```
   structsd tx structs reactor-infuse TX_FLAGS -- [validator-address] [amount]ualpha
   ```
   With no flags this stakes **from your player vault**. `--delegator-address [registered-address]` stakes from that signing key instead; `--owner-id [guild-id]` stakes from a guild vault you have `PermTokenInfuse` authority over. `reactor-infuse` is Tier 1 — commission is locked permanently for that infusion. Defusion takes the same arguments and selectors (`reactor-defuse -- [validator-address] [amount]ualpha`) and starts a cooldown before Alpha returns to the same account it came from; `reactor-cancel-defusion -- [validator-address] [amount]ualpha [creation-height]` re-stakes during that cooldown (and counts as an inflow against the cap).
4. Verify: re-query player; capacity increased. For a large position also check `owner-reactor-diversity` — the applied bonus may have moved.

In current Team Ops, the Infusions surface can preview and execute reactor infuse,
defuse, migration, cancel-defusion, and restart for the primary/registered virtual
players. It re-derives the holder signer, checks the infusion address, validator health,
and projected power headroom before signing. Generator infusions are listed but remain
read-only there because they are irreversible. These `mcp_infusion_*` names are internal
Tauri/web-board commands; `tools/list` still has 13 MCP tools and no
`structs_infusions`.

## Procedure — generator infusion (Tier 2, irreversible)

Only with defense in place. **Approval Block**: struct id is your generator (type 20/21/22, online); amount is annihilated on success (no defusion); the **vault** holds the amount (generator fuel is burned from the player vault, never from the signing key); generator's defense posture is sound (shield up, defenders/PDC, no inbound fleet); `--from` owns it.

```
structsd tx structs struct-generator-infuse TX_FLAGS -- [struct-id] [amount]ualpha
```

Exactly one coin, `ualpha` only. Rates: Field Generator 2 kW/g, Continental Power Plant 5 kW/g, World Engine 10 kW/g. Generator fuel survives the generator going offline (`generatorDisabled: true` on its infusion: fuel and ratio stay, power reads 0) and is credited again when it is reactivated; destruction never refunds it. Generator funding works even while you are browned out — it is one of the few actions that does — which makes it a recovery lever if you accept the irreversibility.

## Procedure — distribute power (substations & allocations)

For pooling power across structs/players (e.g. a guild powering members). Cascading deletes can knock players offline mid-operation — these are Tier 2.

1. Create an allocation from your source: `structsd tx structs allocation-create --allocation-type static|dynamic|automated TX_FLAGS -- [source-id] [power]` (`--controller [owner-id]` optional; a player `1-N` or guild `0-N`). Automated allocations auto-grow with capacity — **one per source**. An allocation sourced from a guild or a guild-owned substation is guild-controlled by default; naming another controller needs admin authority on the source.
2. Create a substation: `structsd tx structs substation-create TX_FLAGS -- [owner-id] [allocation-id]`. The allocation must not already feed a substation — disconnect it first (`substation-allocation-disconnect`) or use a fresh one.
3. Connect/disconnect sources: `substation-allocation-connect|disconnect -- [substation-id] [allocation-id]`.
4. Connect/disconnect players: `substation-player-connect|disconnect -- [substation-id] [player-id]`.
5. Migrate players: `substation-player-migrate -- [substation-id] [player-id,player-id2,...]` (destination substation + player CSV; there is **no** source-substation argument).

> **Connecting/migrating another player needs `PermSubstationConnection` (1024) on the player too — not just the substation.** Connect and migrate run the same two checks (`1024` on the destination substation AND on each target player) and both call `MigrateSubstation`. A player object is owned by itself, so **owning the substation is not enough to move other members**: either the member **self-connects** (they own themselves; gate the substation with `permission-guild-rank-set [sub] [guild] 1024 [rank]`), or they grant you `permission-grant-on-object [player] [you] 1024` first. Repointing the guild entry substation (`guild-update-entry-substation-id`) only reroutes **new** join-proxy members — existing members are not auto-migrated. See [energy.md](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/energy).

**Three things that bite when pooling** (full detail in [energy.md](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/energy)):

- **A substation loses 10% and dilutes the rest evenly.** Only `floor(capacity × 9/10)` of a substation's incoming power is usable; each connected player gets `connectionCapacity = (usable − load) / connectionCount`, recomputed on every connect/disconnect and on every outgoing allocation change. Every new player connection shrinks everyone's share — plan the pool against `connectionCount` and the 90%, not the raw feed.
- **Anyone can contribute to any substation.** `substation-allocation-connect` checks permission only on **your own allocation**, not the destination substation's owner — no guild-owner veto, no membership needed. Contributing is open, but a contributed allocation raises *your own* connection by only `0.9/connectionCount`, so it's community behavior, not self-growth. A substation that is being deleted (`deletion_pending: true`) refuses new connections of any kind.
- **Over-committing triggers a brownout.** If an object's `load` exceeds its usable `capacity` (e.g. a substation loses a feed), the grid **destroys that object's outgoing allocations in creation order** until load fits — cascading downstream and knocking dependents offline. The cascade is bounded to 256 allocation teardowns per block and queues the remainder (FIFO), so a large collapse plays out over several blocks rather than one. Leave headroom.
- **Stored headroom is not admission.** A new allocation, a dynamic increase, or an agreement is validated against the *complete* incoming supply chain (reactor → allocations → substations → you) under a 2,048-object limit. A cycle, an overloaded ancestor, a jailed reactor at the root, or a chain too deep to prove returns `unsupported_supply` even when `capacity − load` reads positive. Simplify the topology; waiting for the cascade does not clear a complexity refusal.

## Offline recovery (emergency)

1. **Free power now** — `struct-deactivate` non-essential structs until `load + structsLoad ≤ capacity + capacitySecondary`. Keep the **Command Ship online** if at all possible (offline CMD ship makes your planet raidable).
2. **Raise capacity** — infuse a reactor (fastest) or open an agreement.
3. **Reactivate** in priority order: Command Ship → defense → production.
4. Note: a player on a substation pool can show `capacity=0` while structs run fine — `structsLoad > 0` is the real "functioning" signal, not `capacity > 0`.

## Commands reference

| Action | Command |
|--------|---------|
| Reactor infuse (from vault; `--delegator-address [addr]` for a registered key, `--owner-id [guild-id]` for a guild vault) | `structsd tx structs reactor-infuse TX_FLAGS -- [validator-addr] [amount]ualpha` |
| Reactor restart | `structsd tx structs reactor-restart TX_FLAGS -- [reactor-address]` |
| Reactor defuse (same selectors) | `structsd tx structs reactor-defuse TX_FLAGS -- [validator-addr] [amount]ualpha` |
| Reactor cancel defusion (same selectors) | `structsd tx structs reactor-cancel-defusion TX_FLAGS -- [validator-addr] [amount]ualpha [creation-height]` |
| Reactor migrate (same selectors) | `structsd tx structs reactor-begin-migration TX_FLAGS -- [src-val] [dest-val] [amount]ualpha` |
| Reactor cap headroom | `structsd query structs reactor-stake-share [reactor-id]` |
| Diversity bonus | `structsd query structs owner-reactor-diversity [owner-id]` |
| Vault address | `structsd query structs vault [owner-id]` |
| Generator infuse (Tier 2, from vault, one coin) | `structsd tx structs struct-generator-infuse TX_FLAGS -- [struct-id] [amount]ualpha` |
| Allocation create / update / delete | `structsd tx structs allocation-create --allocation-type [t] TX_FLAGS -- [source-id] [power]` (and `allocation-update`/`allocation-delete -- [allocation-id] ...`) |
| Substation create / delete | `structsd tx structs substation-create \| substation-delete TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Substation allocation connect/disconnect | `structsd tx structs substation-allocation-connect \| disconnect TX_FLAGS -- [sub-id] [alloc-id]` |
| Substation player connect/disconnect/migrate | `structsd tx structs substation-player-connect \| disconnect \| migrate TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Query player power | `structsd query structs player [id]` |
| Query reactor | `structsd query structs reactor [id]` |
| Query substation / allocations | `structsd query structs substation [id]` / `allocation-all-by-source [id]` |

`TX_FLAGS` per [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html); power ops cascade, so default to interactive even on routine ones. **Requires** [`structsd`](/skills/structsd-install/SKILL.html) on PATH and a signing key.

## Verification

- `structsd query structs player [id]` — `capacity`/`capacitySecondary`/`load`/`structsLoad`, online status.
- `structsd query structs substation [id]` — connected allocations/players.

## Errors

- **Going offline** — load > capacity; deactivate structs, then infuse/buy capacity.
- **"insufficient balance" / affordability on infuse** — the **vault** lacks ualpha (the key's balance is irrelevant). Fund the vault, pass `--delegator-address` (reactors only), refine ore, or buy via agreement.
- **`reactor stake cap exceeded` (1613)** — validator at/over 30% of bonded stake with the cap active; pick another reactor (`reactor-stake-share`).
- **`vault_owner_mismatch`** — an explicit `--delegator-address` does not match the vault selected by `--owner-id`; drop one of the two.
- **Capacity fell after infusing** — diversity bonus shrank because the position concentrated; check `owner-reactor-diversity` and spread across reactors.
- **"generator infuse failed" / invalid amount** — struct isn't a generator (20/21/22), is destroyed, or the amount names more than one coin.
- **`unsupported_supply`** — the allocation's supply chain cannot be proven (cycle, overloaded or jailed ancestor, >2,048 objects). Not a headroom problem; simplify the graph.
- **Allocation exceeds source** — source capacity too small; allocate less or add capacity.
- **Automated allocation limit** — one automated per source; use static/dynamic for more.
- **`substation-create` rejects the allocation** — it already feeds a substation; disconnect it first.
- **`deletion_pending`** — the destination substation is closing; connect elsewhere.

- [knowledge/mechanics/power](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/power) — capacity/load/online quick formula card
- [knowledge/mechanics/resources](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/resources) — Alpha → energy conversion rates
- [playbooks/situations/resource-rich](https://structs.ai/playbooks/situations/resource-rich) — infusion strategy

# Combat skill: attacks, raids, defense

Combat exists to move ore. **Raiding** is how you take another player's mined ore; **attacks** soften defenses and kill structs; **defense** keeps your own ore and infrastructure alive. **Raids steal ore. That's it. Your account is never at risk from raids.** The single most important fact: **raidability is a live state predicate about the defender's fleet and Command Ship — not the shield level number.** The displayed shield value (e.g. 25–125) only sets raid PoW difficulty (a timer). "Shields are up" does not mean "cannot be raided." Gate = `IsDefenderCommandStructVulnerable()` (no owner / no fleet / fleet off-station / no CMD ship / CMD destroyed / CMD offline). Keep your fleet on station with the Command Ship online and you are effectively unraidable; to raid someone, you must **catch them with the gate open — or open it** by destroying (or power-starving) their Command Ship. Vulnerability is a state you can force, not just one to wait for. (The Command Ship only defends home while the fleet is on station, so sending your fleet away to raid opens **your** gate until it returns.)

Conventions (TX_FLAGS, `--` rule, `-D 3` PoW, the per-player charge bar, one-tx-at-a-time) come from [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html). **Interface:** if Structs Desktop MCP is connected, prefer `structs_intel` (`scout`, `valid_targets`, `raid_readiness`, `battle_log`) and `structs_action`/`structs_strike` for engagements — `simulate` and `strike_options` are **struct-scoped** (there is no planet-raid preflight simulator). Use `raid_readiness {only_gaps:true}` before combat to find READY/PARTIAL/BLIND ambit coverage, and `battle_log {category:"all"}` when you need all planet activity rather than only `struct_attack`. The `structsd` commands below are the complete fallback.

## When to use it

- You spotted a target with stored ore and want to raid it.
- You're under attack or expect to be (a refine window, a hostile fleet nearby).
- You need to kill a specific enemy struct (a generator, a defender, a Tank).
- You're setting up standing defense for your planet.

## Decisions

### Two ways to raid: opportunistic vs siege

**Shield-vulnerability is a state you can create, not just one you wait for.** This is the most-missed idea in raiding. There are two modes:

- **Opportunistic** — the defender is *already* vulnerable when you scout (fleet off-station, or Command Ship already offline/destroyed/absent). Move in and grind. Cheap, but truly-vulnerable ore-holders are rare.
- **Siege (force vulnerability)** — the defender is shielded (Command Ship online, fleet on station). You **manufacture** the window: move in, strip same-ambit blockers, **destroy their Command Ship**, then complete before they rebuild. "Their Command Ship is online" is *not* a dead end — it is the thing you go and break.

An online Command Ship should trigger the question **"can I destroy it?"**, not "next target." See the siege procedure below.

### Idle is not vulnerable (and the fleet-move trap)

A **dormant** owner (idle for days) is not a **vulnerable** one. Powered structs stay online with no player action, so an idle owner's Command Ship keeps defending indefinitely — the opportunistic gate stays shut. **Never infer raidability from an inactivity signal or a UI "vulnerable"/"inactive" badge** (those are derived from activity, not the live shield predicate). Confirm the live state: Command Ship online + fleet on station.

The trap this avoids is real and strictly-negative: moving your fleet to a not-yet-vulnerable target drops **your own** shields (fleet off-station) and exposes **your** stored ore, for a raid that can never complete. If you move your fleet, commit to the *siege*, not just the move. (The upside: a dormant owner who holds ore and won't rebuild is the *best* siege target — the window you force open stays open.)

### Raid go/no-go (the most important decision)

Use `scripts/scout.sh [planet-id]` for a structured read, then decide by mode:

1. **Is there ore to take?** — defender **player** `storedOre > 0` (`StoredOreAttributeId` on the player object; do **not** read the planet's `buriedOre`). A successful raid seizes **all** of it at `MsgPlanetRaidComplete` (atomic; no partial loot). No ore → no raid, in either mode.
2. **Is the raidability gate open right now?** — fleet off-station, or Command Ship offline/destroyed/absent. This is **not** the displayed shield number.
   - **Yes → opportunistic go.** Confirm you out-damage the defenders within the window, `blockStartRaid != 0`, and the shield PoW is feasible (base 25, +online defense-struct contributions — that number is a **timer**, not the gate).
   - **No (Command Ship online, fleet on station) → siege decision.** Can you reach and destroy their Command Ship (6 HP, usually defended), and is the ore worth leaving your own home exposed while your fleet is away? A dormant defender who won't rebuild tips this toward go; a watchful, well-defended one tips it toward wait/watch.
3. **Will you survive the resolution and the window?** — your fleet must out-damage the defense, and (for a siege) kill the Command Ship before an active defender rebuilds it.

There is no planet-raid simulator (`simulate`/`strike_options` are struct-scoped). Run the three reads — player `storedOre`, the gate, `blockStartRaid` — per candidate. Do not declare the network empty from a partial sample.

**When NOT to raid**: no/low stored ore; a shield so high the PoW outlasts your window; a well-defended Command Ship guarded by a bloc that will retaliate for less ore than you'd lose; or you cannot reach the Command Ship's ambit. Raiding is an *expedition* — it costs you a fleet locked `away` and your home undefended by fleet. Expected ore must beat that cost. An honest no-go (or "watch and wait") is a win, not a failure.

### Defense doctrine

- **Keep your Command Ship online and your fleet on station — always.** That combination makes you unraidable. Most "I got raided" stories are "my CMD ship went offline (usually power) and I didn't notice" — or "I sent my fleet off to raid and left my own shields down." Watch for it (`scripts/watch-defense.mjs` alerts on your CMD ship dropping and on raids against you). Treat raiding with your own fleet as a deliberate trade: while it's away, your home is exposed.
- **Stack shields.** Orbital Shield Generator and Ore Bunker are unlimited — build several to push raid difficulty up as a second layer behind the CMD-ship gate. Mid-raid: do **not** start a new refine (~34h); only finish one already completable — see [under-attack](https://structs.ai/playbooks/situations/under-attack).
- **Refine fast.** Defense protects *structs*, never *ore*. The only defense for ore is turning it into Alpha Matter ([`structs-production`](/skills/structs-production/SKILL.html)).
- **Assign defenders** across ambits to protect the Command Ship and key structs.

### Desktop autonomous-combat controls

Current Desktop schemas are intentionally small:

- `autoresponse`: `enabled`, `autonomy`, `interval_secs`, `max_shots_per_hour`, `include_primary_shooters`, `now`. It restores/recalls the defender's fleet and fires co-located shooters; the rolling hourly ceiling is the only shot cap.
- `autoraid`: `enabled`, `autonomy`, `posture`, `interval_secs`, `min_ore`, `min_score`, `give_up_after_mins`, `max_concurrent_raids`, `target_cooldown_mins`, `w_ore`, `w_opening`, `w_weakness`, `w_grudge`, `now`. `cautious` uses open windows only; `opportunist` and `aggressive` may siege.

Legacy response modes/per-incident caps, time windows, mid-raid refining, and separate vulnerability/siege gates are not current controls. Evaluate loops with `autonomy:"advise"`; preview-only strike planning is separate. Mid-raid refine is paused by chain v0.21.0, so response hardening recalls/restores the fleet instead.

Decisions live in [`playbooks/situations/under-attack`](https://structs.ai/playbooks/situations/under-attack), [`guild-war`](https://structs.ai/playbooks/situations/guild-war), and [`playbooks/meta/counter-strategies`](https://structs.ai/playbooks/meta/counter-strategies).

## How a raid resolves

`blockStartRaid` is the **defender's vulnerability clock**, and raid PoW age is measured from it:

- It starts when the raidability gate opens — their Command Ship goes offline or their fleet leaves station (or when you arrive to find it already open).
- It resets to 0 if the defender closes the gate (Command Ship back online with the fleet on station) — and completion is rejected (`raid_clock_unset` when 0; the raid status flips to `ongoing` with the gate closed).
- Raid statuses you'll see: `initiated` → `shieldsVulnerable` (gate open, clock running, winnable) → `raidSuccessful` / `attackerRetreated`. `attackerDefeated` means your raiding Command Ship was destroyed while away. `demilitarized` means no defenders to resolve against.

The clock only runs **while your raider is present** at the target — it is set at arrival if the defender is already vulnerable (opportunistic), or the moment their Command Ship drops while you're there (siege). So a raid is a race against the defender noticing and restoring the gate. Scout the CMD ship and fleet position first. For an **opportunistic** raid, don't move your fleet until the gate is already open; for a **siege**, moving in is step one and you open it yourself.

**A raid steals ore.** A successful raid seizes **all** of the defender's `storedOre` (`StoredOreAttributeId` on the **player**) and nothing more — it does not destroy the player or their structs. Settlement is atomic at `MsgPlanetRaidComplete`; there is no partial loot and no refund. Killing the defender's Command Ship opens the `shieldsVulnerable` window so the raid can complete; if the defender restores or rebuilds it before you finish, completion is rejected (`shields_active`) and you get **nothing**. Beware the reverse: `trigger_raid_defeat_by_destruction` is on the Command Ship, so if **your** raiding CMD ship is destroyed while away, your fleet is defeated (`attackerDefeated`) and sent home. Win path for ore: strip same-ambit blockers → destroy the defender's CMD ship → complete the raid before they rebuild it (most reliable vs an offline defender).

## Procedure — opportunistic raid (defender already vulnerable)

1. **Scout** — `scripts/scout.sh [planet-id]` (or `structsd query structs planet [id]` + **player** + struct queries). Confirm the go conditions above: **player** `storedOre`, Command Ship status (offline/destroyed/absent or fleet off-station), and `blockStartRaid`. Do not treat the planet's buried ore or the shield number as the loot or the gate.
2. **Optional stealth** — stealth a unit before approach (`struct-stealth-activate`, 2 charge); attacking later auto-drops it.
3. **Move fleet to the target** (instant). Your fleet (and your Command Ship) is now `away`; you can't build/mine at home while away, **and your own planet's shields are now vulnerable** until the fleet returns — refine your home ore before you leave.
   ```
   structsd tx structs fleet-move TX_FLAGS -- [fleet-id] [destination-location-id]
   ```
4. **Approval Block** — fleet is your raider and now at the target; defender's CMD ship is down (verified); your home ore is refined or below your theft tolerance; you accept an auto-submitted completion landing minutes-to-hours out.
5. **Raid compute** (expedition, auto-submits completion — the documented `-y` exception):
   ```bash
   nohup structsd tx structs planet-raid-compute -D 3 --from [key] --gas auto --gas-adjustment 1.5 -y -- [fleet-id] \
     > memory/jobs/raid-[fleet-id].log 2>&1 & echo $! > memory/jobs/raid-[fleet-id].pid
   ```
6. **Move fleet home and refine the stolen ore immediately** — it's stealable in *your* hands now too.

If the defender restores their Command Ship mid-raid, the clock resets — withdraw or wait for it to drop again.

## Procedure — siege raid (force the window open)

Use this when the target holds ore but is shielded (Command Ship online, fleet on station) — the case an opportunistic raid can't touch. It costs a fleet engagement and leaves your home exposed, so run the go/no-go above first. Best against a dormant defender who won't rebuild.

1. **Scout the Command Ship's ambit and defenders** — `scripts/scout.sh [planet-id]` surfaces the defender's Command Ship id and status; query it directly with `structsd query structs struct [commandStruct-id]` for its `operatingAmbit`. To enumerate the **same-ambit** structs that can block for it, use the Guild Stack ("defenders by planet" — there is no `structsd` CLI command that lists a planet's structs). Confirm you have weapons that reach the Command Ship's ambit.
2. **Refine your own ore and move your fleet to the target.** Your home shields drop while away — accept that exposure as the cost of the siege. A planet holds **one visiting fleet** by default; if the slot is taken, `fleet-move` is `queue_full`.
   ```
   structsd tx structs fleet-move TX_FLAGS -- [fleet-id] [destination-location-id]
   ```
   At this point `planet-raid-compute` will still reject (`no active raid window`) — that is expected; the window isn't open yet.
3. **Strip same-ambit blockers, then destroy the Command Ship** with `struct-attack` (space repeated attacks; the charge bar is per-player and doesn't bank — coordinate multiple accounts to focus-fire if you have them). Destroying it fires the chain's vulnerability hook and opens `shieldsVulnerable` with your raider present.
   ```
   structsd tx structs struct-attack TX_FLAGS -- [operating-struct-id] [target-id] [weapon-system]
   ```
4. **Verify the window is open** — `structsd query structs planet [planet-id]` shows `blockStartRaid != 0` (raid status `shieldsVulnerable`). Only now is compute worthwhile.
5. **Raid compute** (same command as opportunistic step 5), then **move home and refine** the seized ore immediately.

Watch for the defender rebuilding the Command Ship (an active defender will) — if it comes back online with the fleet on station before your proof lands, the clock resets and completion fails. Never let **your** raiding Command Ship die while away (`attackerDefeated`).

For Desktop `structs_hash start`, RAID and BUILD require the real `block_start`; the hasher refuses to guess because a current-block anchor always produces a chain-rejected proof. MINE/REFINE may omit it: Desktop resolves the struct's planet and reads the shared planet ore clock.

## Procedure — direct attack

Scout the target's ambit and defense type, position (Command Ship only) into range, then fire. The attack needs only the attacking struct and its owner online — your Command Ship does not need to be online to attack, change defenders, or change stealth. The **target must be a built struct**: a struct that is still building cannot be attacked (`unbuilt`), and a destroyed one is rejected (`destroyed`); the target's online status is irrelevant. The CLI prompts; verify target IDs and that you aren't crossing guild lines you didn't intend to (attacking another guild's structs is a Tier 2 act of war). Note most weapons are single-target (`primaryWeaponTargets = 1`) — the comma list only spreads damage for weapons whose target count is > 1.

**Planner false-negative fallback.** `structs_strike` and `structs_intel {query:"strike_options"}` are advisers, not chain authority. A 2026-09-24 playtest saw both report “no reach” while an online, land-operating Mobile Artillery was co-located with a land Command Ship; the direct attack succeeded. Before accepting an “unreachable” verdict, refresh the raw attacker, target, and fleet records and independently confirm:

1. attacker is built, online, not destroyed, and its owner is online;
2. attacker and target resolve to the same **planet** (a fleet struct's `locationId` is a fleet id, so follow that fleet's `locationId` to the planet);
3. the selected weapon's reach bitmask includes the target's current `operatingAmbit`;
4. target is built, not destroyed, and not hidden from that attacker.

If all four hold, the planner refusal is a Desktop bug or stale-cache result, not proof that the chain will reject. Use the ordinary `struct-attack` action/preflight and let the chain arbitrate; record the planner output plus the fresh raw reads for a bug report. This fallback does **not** waive normal approval or rules of engagement.

```
structsd tx structs struct-attack TX_FLAGS -- [operating-struct-id] [target-id,target-id2,...] [weapon-system]
```

Attacks cost 3-5 charge from your **per-player** bar; space repeated attacks accordingly.

## Procedure — defense setup

```
structsd tx structs struct-defense-set TX_FLAGS -- [defender-struct-id] [protected-struct-id]
structsd tx structs struct-defense-clear TX_FLAGS -- [defender-struct-id]
```

**Only fleet structs can be assigned as a defender** (`canDefend: true`; 1 charge each; stagger ~6 s on one key) as long as the defender is **built, online, and co-located** with the protected struct — ambit is **not** required to *assign*. Planetary types (Ore Extractor, Refinery, Ore Bunker, PDC, generators, …) are rejected. Ambit decides what the defender can do: **same-ambit** is required only to **block** (intercept a hit), while a **cross-ambit** defender still **counters** whenever its weapon can reach the attacker. Spread fleet defenders across ambits for counter coverage; keep same-ambit defenders where you need real interception. Minimum viable defense: at least one combat struct per ambit guarding the Command Ship (6 HP; most fleet structs are 3 HP).

## Tactical reference

### Targeting (which struct hits which ambit)

| Struct | Lives In | Primary | Secondary |
|--------|----------|---------|-----------|
| Command Ship | Any (movable) | current ambit only | — |
| Battleship | Space | Land, Water (**armour-piercing**) | Space |
| Starfighter | Space | Space | Space (Attack Run, ≥1 hit) |
| Frigate | Space | Space, Air | — |
| Pursuit Fighter | Air | Air | — |
| Stealth Bomber | Air | Land, Water | — |
| High Alt Interceptor | Air | Space, Air | — |
| Mobile Artillery | Land | Land, Water | — |
| Tank | Land | Land | — |
| SAM Launcher | Land | Space, Air | — |
| Cruiser | Water | Land, Water | Air |
| Destroyer | Water | Air, Water | — |
| Submersible | Water | Space, Water | — |

The Command Ship is the only struct that can change ambits (`struct-move`); it attacks only its current ambit. Reposition it into range to attack, or out of range to hide.

### Weapon control vs defense (evasion + armour-piercing)

| Target Defense | vs Guided | vs Unguided |
|----------------|-----------|-------------|
| Signal Jamming (Battleship, Pursuit Fighter, Cruiser) | **66% miss** | full hit |
| Defensive Maneuver (High Alt Interceptor) | full hit | **66% miss** |
| Armour (Tank, Field Generator, Continental Power Plant, World Engine) | full hit, −1 dmg | full hit, −1 dmg |
| Stealth Mode (Stealth Bomber, Submersible) | same-ambit only | same-ambit only |
| Indirect Combat (Mobile Artillery) | full hit | full hit |
| None | full hit | full hit |

Use unguided vs Signal Jamming, guided vs Defensive Maneuver. **Armour reduces damage by 1 — except against armour-piercing weapons (the Battleship primary), which ignore it.** The Battleship is the dedicated answer to Tanks and to the (now armoured) power generators. Minimum damage after reduction is always 1.

### Combat resolution notes

- **Counters are ambit-gated, blocks are ambit-matched.** A defender counters whenever its weapon can reach the **attacker's** ambit (regardless of what it's defending); it can only **block** when it shares the **target's** ambit. Consequence: attacking land structs from air/water/space (an ambit the defenders can't reach) takes **zero counter damage** — the single biggest combat lever. Pick your attacking ambit to dodge counters.
- Each struct counters at most **once per `struct-attack` invocation** (not per target/shot). Defender counter fires before block and even on evaded shots; target counter fires after all shots (destroyed targets can't counter).
- Block only fires on non-evaded shots and only from a defender in the **target's** ambit.
- **Counters are a backstop, not a damage plan** — counter values are small (typically 1; Command Ship 2) and a cross-ambit attacker takes none at all. Win with active `struct-attack` volleys from a safe ambit, not by baiting counters.
- **Single-target**: every weapon has `primaryWeaponTargets = 1` (one struct per volley) — no multi-target weapon exists. The comma-list in `struct-attack` doesn't make a single-target weapon spread.
- **No charge banking**: any action resets your shared charge bar to 0 and it refills ~1/block — you cannot stockpile for a multi-attack burst. Plan combat as spaced single actions. Because the bar is **per-player**, the way to land many hits at once is **parallel**: coordinate multiple accounts to focus-fire one target — N players land N attacks per charge cycle. See [team-operations](https://structs.ai/playbooks/meta/team-operations).
- **Planetary defenses (attacking a planet)**: the **Jamming Satellite** runs a low-orbit ballistic interceptor network that can **evade your _guided_ ordnance against planetary structs on their own planet — regardless of ambit** (`evadedByPlanetaryDefenses`). Ambit no longer matters and **unguided ordnance passes through untouched**, so bring unguided weapons against a planet with interceptors, or expect 0s from guided fire. This is on top of any unit-level `signalJamming` the target itself carries (both layers stack against guided). The PDC and the interceptor network are the planetary defenses that affect combat.
- PDC auto-fires after all targets resolve (it does not counter); multiple players' PDCs stack.
- A successful raid seizes **all** of the defender's `storedOre` and nothing else — there is no player-elimination outcome (see raid section). Destroyed structs are gone forever but can be rebuilt (full PoW). Losing your Command Ship disables the whole fleet until you build a new one — protect it above all, and never let your raiding CMD ship die while away (`attackerDefeated`).

## Commands reference

| Action | CLI Command |
|--------|-------------|
| Attack | `structsd tx structs struct-attack TX_FLAGS -- [struct-id] [target-ids] [weapon-system]` |
| Raid compute (PoW + auto-complete) | `structsd tx structs planet-raid-compute -D 3 TX_FLAGS_APPROVED -- [fleet-id]` |
| Raid complete (manual, rare) | `structsd tx structs planet-raid-complete TX_FLAGS -- [fleet-id] [proof] [nonce]` |
| Fleet move | `structsd tx structs fleet-move TX_FLAGS -- [fleet-id] [destination-location-id]` |
| Defense set / clear | `structsd tx structs struct-defense-set \| struct-defense-clear TX_FLAGS -- [defender-id] [protected-id]` |
| Stealth on / off | `structsd tx structs struct-stealth-activate \| struct-stealth-deactivate TX_FLAGS -- [struct-id]` |
| Move Command Ship (ambit) | `structsd tx structs struct-move TX_FLAGS -- [cmd-ship-id] [ambit] [slot] [location]` |

Raid flow: scout → (CMD ship down?) → fleet-move → raid-compute → fleet-move home → refine. `planet-raid-compute` is the documented `-y` exception; your Approval Block is the gate. `planet-raid-complete` does not consume charge.

**Requires**: [`structsd`](/skills/structsd-install/SKILL.html) on PATH and a signing key.

## Verification

- `structsd query structs fleet [id]` — location and `onStation`/`away`.
- After a raid: your `storedOre` rose (refine it). For the exact grams seized, the **authoritative source is `ledger` rows with `action = 'seized'`**, not `planet_raid.seized_ore` — the ledger even records 0-gram seizures (a raid that reached the planet but took nothing, e.g. a repelled probe). See [database-schema.md — planet_raid](https://structs.ai/knowledge/infrastructure/database-schema).
- A `raidSuccessful` event plus the ore ledger/state delta proves settlement. Do **not** require a Desktop `tx_settled` row for an auto-submitted raid proof: that synthetic receipt is produced by the MCP action bridge, and PoW completions can bypass it. To recover the completion tx hash, query Tendermint/Cosmos transactions at the raid-success block and select the tx carrying `EventHashSuccess(category=raid, objectId=[fleet-id], planetId=[planet-id])` plus `EventRaid(status=raidSuccessful)`. See [chain-events — recovering a PoW completion hash](https://structs.ai/api/chain-events#recovering-a-pow-completion-transaction-hash).
- After attacks: events include remaining-health values — use them to assess damage.
- Broadcast ≠ success: a raid can land but resolve as `defeat`/`ongoing`. Query the raid status.

## Errors

- **"shields are not vulnerable: no active raid window (defending Command Ship may still be online)"** — the CLI-side `planet-raid-compute` pre-check when `blockStartRaid == 0`. This is the message you usually hit first. It does **not** mean "grind harder": the defender is shielded. Either wait/watch for them to slip (opportunistic), or open the window yourself by destroying their Command Ship with your fleet present (siege procedure above).
- **"cannot raid_complete while shields_active" / raid rejected** — the chain-side `planet-raid-complete` rejection: the defender is not vulnerable at completion (fleet on station with the Command Ship online). You cannot win until they're vulnerable again — force it or wait.
- **"cannot raid_complete while raid_clock_unset"** — `blockStartRaid` is 0 (no live raid window). Get your fleet to the target and make the defender vulnerable (their CMD ship offline/destroyed, or fleet off-station) before computing.
- **"unbuilt" / "destroyed" (attack)** — the target struct isn't a valid combat target: it's still building or already destroyed. Pick a built target.
- **"unreachable" / "out_of_range"** — your weapon can't reach that ambit; reposition the Command Ship or use a different struct.
- **"fleet not away"** — move the fleet to the target first.
- **"insufficient charge"** — per-player bar too low; wait (see conventions).
- **Charge already used this block (ante 2021) / duplicate charge in tx (2020)** — attacks, moves, defense and stealth changes are charge messages: one per player per block, never two in one transaction. Space them ~6 s; parallelism comes from more players, not more messages.
- **"queue_full"** — the destination planet already has its visiting-fleet cap (`1 + locationListExtra`, default 1). Wait for the parked fleet to leave, or pick another target.
- **"cannot defend" / StructCannotDefend** — you tried to assign a planetary struct as a defender. Only fleet types (`canDefend: true`) work.
- **`self_defense`** — a struct cannot be assigned to defend itself; pick another protected struct.
- **Completed planet as `fleet-move` destination** — a mined-out planet is unreachable and unraidable. Its former owner's `storedOre` is not a target; find where they went instead.
- **Fleet id rejected** — fleet ids are exactly `9-<decimal>`; `9-01` is not `9-1`.
- **"under_raid"** — mine/refine is paused while a visitor heads the queue. Do not retry those computes until they leave.

# Commerce skill: energy, banks, transfers

Commerce is how Alpha Matter compounds into economic power. The core loop: refine Alpha → infuse a reactor (capacity) → route it through an **allocation** to a **substation** → sell it through a **provider** → buyers pay in tokens via **agreements** → reinvest. Layered on top are guild Central Bank tokens (mint/redeem) and direct transfers. Where [`structs-energy`](/skills/structs-energy/SKILL.html) is "power my own structs", this skill is "make Alpha and energy *earn*."

Conventions (TX_FLAGS, `--` rule, charge bar, one-tx-at-a-time, `ualpha` denom suffix, the vault) are in [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html). Every command here is Tier 1 or Tier 2 — default to interactive.

> **Every spend in this skill is paid from a vault, not from your signing key.** Agreement collateral, reactor stake, Central Bank mint/redeem/convert and rank purchases all debit the player vault (or a guild vault you control). Fund the vault first (`structsd tx bank send [key] [vault-address] [amount]ualpha`; address from `structsd query structs vault [owner-id]`). Earnings likewise land in vaults: refined Alpha, redeemed Alpha, minted guild tokens. The one exception is `provider-withdraw-balance`, which pays to the bank address you name.

## When to use it

- You have surplus capacity and want revenue (run a provider).
- You need capacity but have no Alpha (buy via agreement).
- You're setting provider pricing / access policy.
- You want to stake Alpha into a reactor for capacity, mint/redeem guild tokens, or transfer tokens.

## Decisions

**Sell or hold?** Surplus capacity earns nothing idle. If you have headroom beyond your own structs, sell it. Price in **guild tokens** (`1uguild.0-N`) to create demand for your guild's currency, or in `ualpha` for direct value.

**Buyer-side: shop before you commit.** Opening an agreement **debits the entire cost in full, immediately, at open** — `rate × capacity × duration`, moved from the paying vault into the collateral pool (`x/structs/keeper/msg_server_agreement_open.go`). It is not metered per block. Closing early can incur a penalty. Compare providers on `rateAmount`, `capacityMaximum`, `durationMaximum`, and penalties before opening. Pick a duration whose expiry height is not already full: at most 256 agreements may expire at one height, and a full bucket rejects the open with `expiration_height_full` — nudge the duration by a block or two and retry.

**The `rate_denom` trap.** The cost is charged in the **provider's** `rate_denom`, not in alpha. A provider that prices in a guild token (`uguild.0-N`) requires your vault to hold that token — a buyer holding only `ualpha` is **rejected at broadcast** (insufficient-funds error keyed `agreement_open`; read `rawLog` for the exact denom). Check the provider's `rateDenom` and acquire that denom (mint guild tokens / trade) *before* opening.

**Reactor staking economics — you are buying *capacity*, not a yield.** Infusing a reactor stakes your Alpha behind a validator at a locked commission and, in return, credits **energy capacity** to you (`1 − commission` of the infused amount; the commission share becomes the reactor's own capacity), plus a **diversity bonus** of up to 50% for stake spread evenly across ten or more reactors. There is **no delegator reward stream, no APR, no passive income** — the payoff is the capacity itself. Income is *indirect*: you turn that capacity into revenue only by selling it as energy through a provider. Lower commission = more capacity to you; spreading across reactors = more bonus; staking also strengthens the guild's reactor. It's reversible only via a defusion cooldown — don't stake Alpha you'll need short-term. A jailed validator zeros the infusion ratio until unjail / `reactor-restart`, and a reactor already holding 30% of bonded stake refuses new stake once the cap is active (`reactor-stake-share`). See [`structs-energy`](/skills/structs-energy/SKILL.html) for the diversity table and cap, and [energy — reactor infusion](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/energy) for the 96/4 split.

**The energy flywheel (advanced default):** mine → refine → infuse guild reactor → automated allocation grows substation capacity → sell via provider for guild tokens → redeem/reinvest. Each turn compounds. Decisions live in [`knowledge/economy/valuation`](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/valuation), [`trading`](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/trading), and [`playbooks/phases/late-game`](https://structs.ai/playbooks/phases/late-game).

## Allocation types (the routing primitive)

| Type | Updatable | Deletable | Auto-grows | Limit | Use |
|------|-----------|-----------|------------|-------|-----|
| static | no | no (while connected) | no | unlimited | fixed routing |
| dynamic | yes | yes | no | unlimited | flexible/managed routing |
| automated | yes | no | yes (with source capacity) | **one per source** | energy sales (recommended) |
| provider-agreement | system | system | system | system-created | auto-made when agreements open — never create manually |

Only the **controller** can delete/transfer an allocation (`--controller [owner-id]` on create, defaults to the creating player; `allocation-transfer -- [allocation-id] [new-controller-owner-id]` to hand it to another player `1-N` or a guild `0-N`). Allocations sourced from a guild or a guild-owned substation default to guild control.

## Procedure — sell energy (provider pipeline)

1. **Have capacity** — infuse a reactor first ([`structs-energy`](/skills/structs-energy/SKILL.html)).
2. **Automated allocation** (auto-grows as you infuse more):
   ```
   structsd tx structs allocation-create --allocation-type automated TX_FLAGS -- [your-player-id] [power]
   ```
3. **Substation** (distribution node):
   ```
   structsd tx structs substation-create TX_FLAGS -- [your-player-id] [allocation-id]
   ```
4. **Provider** (your storefront):
   ```
   structsd tx structs provider-create TX_FLAGS -- [substation-id] [rate] [access-policy] [provider-penalty] [consumer-penalty] [cap-min] [cap-max] [dur-min] [dur-max]
   ```
   Pricing/policy heuristics: `rate` `1uguild.0-N` (drives guild-token demand) or a `ualpha` rate; `access-policy` `open-market` (max reach), `guild-market` (members at/above a rank — grant via `permission-guild-rank-set [provider-id] [guild-id] 262144 [rank]`), or `closed-market` (explicit PermProviderOpen only); penalties `0` initially to lower friction; cap/dur ranges wide (e.g. `1000`–`1000000000` / `100`–`1000000`). Add `--owner-id [guild-id]` to create the provider **as the guild** (needs `PermSourceAllocation` on the guild); otherwise you own it.
5. **Monitor & withdraw**: `structsd query structs provider [id]`; `provider-withdraw-balance TX_FLAGS -- [provider-id] [destination-address]`. Earnings drip from the provider's collateral (escrow) to its earnings address as blocks pass.

> **Deleting the substation under a provider**: `substation-delete` is bounded work — the substation flips to `deletion_pending`, refuses new connections, and the grid unwinds it over several blocks. Inbound agreements are **detached, not closed**: the consumer keeps paying until they `agreement-close`. Warn consumers before you delete.

## Procedure — buy energy (agreement)

1. Find a provider: `structsd query structs provider-all` (or your guild's). Compare rate/capacity/duration/penalties.
2. Open (paid upfront from your vault; auto-creates a provider-agreement allocation):
   ```
   structsd tx structs agreement-open TX_FLAGS -- [provider-id] [duration-in-blocks] [capacity]
   ```
   `--owner-id [guild-id]` opens it on the guild's behalf, paying from the guild vault (needs `PermTokenTransfer` on the guild).
3. Connect the allocation to your substation:
   ```
   structsd tx structs substation-allocation-connect TX_FLAGS -- [substation-id] [allocation-id]
   ```
4. Adjust as needed: `agreement-capacity-increase|decrease`, `agreement-duration-increase`; `agreement-close [agreement-id]` (may penalize).

## Procedure — reactor staking

```
structsd tx structs reactor-infuse TX_FLAGS -- [validator-address] [amount]ualpha
```
Validator address is `structsvaloper1...` (from `structsd query structs reactor [id]`, `validator` field) — not the reactor ID. The stake comes from your **player vault**; `--delegator-address [registered-address]` stakes from a signing key instead, `--owner-id [guild-id]` stakes from a guild vault (needs `PermTokenInfuse` on the guild). Commission locks at infusion. Check `reactor-stake-share [reactor-id]` for cap headroom first. Unstake: `reactor-defuse -- [validator-address] [amount]ualpha` (cooldown; Alpha returns to the account it came from); `reactor-cancel-defusion -- [validator-address] [amount]ualpha [creation-height]` to re-stake during cooldown; `reactor-begin-migration -- [src-val] [dest-val] [amount]ualpha` to move stake (verify the destination — no undo; the destination's cap applies). After an unjail, `reactor-restart [reactor-address]` resyncs energy output from live staking if hooks did not.

## Procedure — guild Central Bank & transfers

- **Mint** (guild-privileged; `guild-bank-mint -- [alpha-amount] [token-amount]`, `--guild-id` to name a guild other than your own): Alpha collateral moves **from the guild vault** to the bank pool and the new tokens land **in the guild vault**. Distribute them with `vault-send` or `player-send` from the guild vault.
- **Redeem** (`guild-bank-redeem -- [amount]uguild.[id] [min-amount-alpha]`, `floor` payout): tokens are burned from your player vault, Alpha arrives in your player vault.
- **Convert** ualpha→token or token→token (`guild-bank-convert`/`guild-bank-convert-token`, `min-amount-token` slippage): debits and credits your player vault. See [`structs-guild`](/skills/structs-guild/SKILL.html) and [`knowledge/economy/guild-banking`](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/guild-banking). `uguild.*` cannot go to IBC.
- **Transfer tokens, vault to vault**: `vault-send TX_FLAGS -- [owner-id] [recipient-owner-id] [amount]` — the game-native payment rail (player `1-N` or guild `0-N` on either side; needs `PermTokenTransfer` on the sending owner).
- **Transfer tokens to or from an address**: `player-send TX_FLAGS -- [from-address] [to-address] [amount]`. `from-address` may be your own registered key *or* a vault address you control — that is how you fund a key with refined Alpha. A typo in the destination is permanent — to a brand-new address this is Tier 2. Guild denoms additionally require an eligible recipient.
- **Buy a guild rank**: when a guild has enabled rank purchase, `guild-rank-purchase TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [target-rank] [max-price] [expected-rank]` pays **in that guild's token** (`uguild.<id>`, base units) from your player vault to the guild vault (`quoted_price_exceeded` if the live price has moved above `max-price`). Hold the token first — redeem/convert into it. Non-members use `guild-membership-join-by-rank-purchase`. Pricing lives in [`structs-guild`](/skills/structs-guild/SKILL.html).

## Commands reference

| Action | Command |
|--------|---------|
| Allocation create / update / delete / transfer | `structsd tx structs allocation-create --allocation-type [t] TX_FLAGS -- [source-id] [power]` (+ `allocation-update`/`allocation-delete -- [allocation-id] ...`; `allocation-transfer -- [allocation-id] [new-controller-owner-id]`) |
| Substation create | `structsd tx structs substation-create TX_FLAGS -- [owner-id] [allocation-id]` |
| Provider create / delete / withdraw | `structsd tx structs provider-create [--owner-id guild] \| provider-delete \| provider-withdraw-balance TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Agreement open / close / adjust | `structsd tx structs agreement-open [--owner-id guild] \| agreement-close \| agreement-capacity-increase \| ... TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Reactor infuse / defuse / migrate / restart | `structsd tx structs reactor-infuse \| reactor-defuse TX_FLAGS -- [validator-addr] [amount]ualpha`; `reactor-begin-migration -- [src-val] [dest-val] [amount]ualpha`; `reactor-restart -- [reactor-addr]` (`--delegator-address` / `--owner-id` select the funding account) |
| Bank mint / redeem | `structsd tx structs guild-bank-mint TX_FLAGS -- [alpha-amount] [token-amount]` (add `--guild-id` to name another guild) / `guild-bank-redeem TX_FLAGS -- [amount]uguild.[id] [min-amount-alpha]` |
| Bank convert / convert-token | `structsd tx structs guild-bank-convert TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [alpha-amount] [min-amount-token]` / `guild-bank-convert-token TX_FLAGS -- [amount]uguild.[src] [target-guild-id] [min-amount-token]` |
| Vault → vault transfer | `structsd tx structs vault-send TX_FLAGS -- [owner-id] [recipient-owner-id] [amount]` |
| Address transfer (key or vault as `from`) | `structsd tx structs player-send TX_FLAGS -- [from-address] [to-address] [amount]` |
| Rank purchase | `structsd tx structs guild-rank-purchase TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [target-rank] [max-price] [expected-rank]` |
| Query provider / agreement / reactor / vault | `structsd query structs provider \| agreement \| reactor \| vault [id]` |
| Query reactor cap / diversity | `structsd query structs reactor-stake-share [reactor-id]` / `owner-reactor-diversity [owner-id]` |

`TX_FLAGS` per [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html). **Requires** [`structsd`](/skills/structsd-install/SKILL.html) on PATH and a signing key.

## Verification

- Provider: `structsd query structs provider [id]` — capacity, rate, active agreements, balance.
- Agreement: `structsd query structs agreement [id]` — status (OPEN→ACTIVE→EXPIRED), capacity, duration.
- Reactor: `structsd query structs reactor [id]` — infused amount, defusion cooldown.
- Player: `structsd query structs player [id]` — `playerInventory.rocks` is vault-spendable Alpha; `structsd query bank balances [vault-address]` for every denom.

## Errors

- **Insufficient balance / affordability** — the **vault** is short in the required denom; the signing key's balance is irrelevant. Refine ore, fund the vault, or acquire the token.
- **`expiration_height_full`** — 256 agreements already expire at that height; change the duration by a block.
- **`reactor stake cap exceeded` (1613)** — reactor at the 30% cap; pick another (`reactor-stake-share`).
- **`quoted_price_exceeded`** — the rank price moved above your `max-price`; re-quote and retry.
- **Provider capacity exceeded** — reduce agreement capacity or add provider capacity.
- **Defusion cooldown** — `reactor-cancel-defusion` to re-stake, or wait it out.
- **recipient_not_eligible** — `uguild.*` cannot go to IBC escrow or an unregistered address.
- **`vault_owner_mismatch`** — `--delegator-address` and `--owner-id` point at different owners; use one.
- **Automated allocation limit** — one per source; use dynamic for additional routing.
- **Generator infuse / staking irreversibility** — staking has a cooldown; generator infusion has none (see [`structs-energy`](/skills/structs-energy/SKILL.html)).

- [api/webapp/analytics](https://structs.ai/api/webapp/analytics) — live `GET /api/guild-bank`, inventory, leaderboards
- [knowledge/economy/valuation](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/valuation) / [trading](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/trading) — what things are worth
- [playbooks/phases/late-game](https://structs.ai/playbooks/phases/late-game) — market control
- [structs-energy](/skills/structs-energy/SKILL.html) — capacity for your own use; [structs-permissions](/skills/structs-permissions/SKILL.html) — provider access grants

# Guild skill: join, ranks, Central Bank

A guild is your faction: it gives you a reactor to infuse, a substation to draw power from, a market to sell into, a token to mint, and allies (or moderators). For a new player, **which guild you join is one of your most consequential early choices** — it shapes your power source, your economy, and who has your back. This skill covers choosing/joining, running a guild, ranks/permissions, identity moderation, and the Central Bank.

Conventions (TX_FLAGS, `--` rule, charge bar, one-tx-at-a-time) are in [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html).

## When to use it

- New player deciding which guild to join (or whether to go solo).
- Creating or administering a guild.
- Managing members, ranks, or moderating member identity.
- Minting/redeeming guild tokens or managing Central Bank collateral.

## Decisions

**Choosing a guild (beginner)** — evaluate candidates on:
- **Reactor commission** — lower = more capacity per gram you infuse (`structsd query structs reactor [id]`).
- **Join requirements** — `joinInfusionMinimum` you must meet (or get an invite to bypass), or — if `joinByRankPurchaseEnabled` — a paid entry (`guild-membership-join-by-rank-purchase`) that needs no stake at all.
- **Treasury** — `structsd query structs vault [guild-id]` then `bank balances`: a guild with Alpha and its own token in the vault can fund members and back its token.
- **Activity & size** — `guild-all` then inspect members; an active guild means a working market and defenders.
- **Token economy** — a guild whose token is actually used (providers priced in it) makes your earnings liquid.
- **Politics** — see [`knowledge/lore/factions`](https://structs.ai/knowledge/lore/factions) and your standing-orders. Joining a guild at war inherits its enemies.

A guild is rarely a trap, but its moderators gain reach into your name/pfp while you're a member (see UGC below). If you dislike a policy, you can leave.

**Creating a guild (advanced)** is a **paid founding**: `guild-create -- [reactor-id] [endpoint] [entry-substation-id]` costs **2,000,000 ualpha from the founder's player vault** — 1,000,000 is burned and 1,000,000 becomes the new guild's Central Bank collateral, which mints **1,000,000 base units of `uguild.<new-id>` into the guild vault**. The named reactor's validator must exist and not be jailed; the entry substation (if given) must be one you can manage connections on. A founder who **owns** a guild must transfer it first (`is_owner`); founding leaves your current guild if you are only a member. There is no proof-of-work and no third-party path; a `guild-create` that carries any legacy proof field is rejected (`legacy_charter_fields_not_supported`). This is Tier 2 — 1M Alpha is annihilated and the rest is locked as collateral.

## Rank system

Numeric ranks, **lower number = higher privilege**:

| Rank | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 1 | Maximum (guild creator) |
| 2–100 | Custom ranks assigned by leadership |
| 101 | Default on join |
| 0 | Unset |

Assigning ranks (`player-update-guild-rank`) is an administration action: the guild owner, or a player holding a **direct** `PermAdmin` grant on the guild, with `PermAdmin` on the **signing key** — a rank register never confers it, so a purchased or assigned rank gives access but not the power to hand out free ranks. Kicking is rank-relative instead: a member can only kick members whose rank is strictly **worse** (higher number) than their own. Rank-permissions (granting a permission to everyone at/above a rank) are the scalable way to delegate — see [`structs-permissions`](/skills/structs-permissions/SKILL.html).

### Selling ranks (optional revenue)

A guild may put ranks up for sale in its own token. Admins configure the curve with `guild-update-rank-purchase -- [guild-id] [base-price] [step-increase] [minimum-rank] [join-by-rank-purchase-enabled]` (`PermAdmin` on the guild). `minimum-rank` is the best rank money can buy (0 disables sales entirely); the n-th step above the entry rank costs `base-price + (n−1) × step-increase` in `uguild.<id>` base units, and a buyer pays the difference between the cumulative price of their target and of their current rank. Payment moves from the buyer's vault to the guild vault. Members buy with `guild-rank-purchase -- [guild-id] [target-rank] [max-price] [expected-rank]` (`expected-rank` is their current rank; `rank_changed` if it moved). If `join-by-rank-purchase-enabled` is true, non-members can enter directly at a purchased rank with `guild-membership-join-by-rank-purchase -- [guild-id] [target-rank] [max-price]` (pass `--expected-guild-id` with your current guild id, or leave it empty if you have none), skipping the infusion minimum; they are migrated to the entry substation like any other joiner. Every sale emits `EventGuildRankPurchase`. Selling your top ranks hands out their rank-permissions — set `minimum-rank` with that in mind.

## Procedure

### Join

1. Discover: `structsd query structs guild-all`, then `guild [id]` and `reactor [id]` for the candidates.
2. Meet the infusion minimum (or secure an invite). Join:
   ```
   structsd tx structs guild-membership-join TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [infusion-id,...]
   ```
   You get the default entry rank (101). Flows: **invite** (`guild-membership-invite` → invitee `...-invite-approve`/`-deny`), **request** (`guild-membership-request` → owner `...-request-approve`/`-deny`), **proxy** (a guild signs you in: `guild-membership-join-proxy -- [address] [proof-pubkey] [proof-signature]`, with optional `--substation-id`, `--player-name`, `--player-pfp`, `--player-pfp-client-render-attributes`), **paid** (`guild-membership-join-by-rank-purchase`, above). Permission gates: a join that must migrate your stake into the guild's reactor needs `PermTokenMigrate` on your signing key; a join that bypasses the minimum via invite/request needs `PermGuildMembership` on the key; a proxy join for an **already-registered** address needs `PermGuildMembership` on that address. Joins and migrations into a guild whose entry substation is closing (`deletion_pending`) are refused.

### Administer

- **Ranks**: `player-update-guild-rank TX_FLAGS -- [player-id] [rank]` (owner or direct `PermAdmin` grant on the guild, and PermAdmin on your signing key; the target must already be a member — add `--guild-id` if you administer a guild you are not a member of); `guild-update-entry-rank TX_FLAGS -- [rank]` (same admin check; a member cannot set the entry rank better than their own); `guild-update-rank-purchase` to sell ranks (above).
- **Membership**: `guild-membership-kick -- [player-id]` (the guild is implicit in the target player). Kicking strips rank-derived access but **preserves direct permission grants** the player holds on guild objects — revoke those explicitly (`permission-revoke-on-object`) if the departure is hostile. Invite/request approve/deny/revoke as above.
- **Settings**: `guild-update-endpoint`, `guild-update-entry-substation-id`, `guild-update-join-infusion-minimum` (+ `-by-invite`/`-by-request`; unknown bypass-level values are denied), `guild-update-owner-id` (Tier 2 — transfers the guild and **clears the outgoing owner's guild membership row**: the old owner is no longer a member unless re-admitted). Invite/request **approve** and **accept** require a pending application — they do not create one.
- **Treasury**: the guild vault (`structsd query structs vault [guild-id]`) holds founding tokens, mint output and rank-sale revenue. Spend it with `vault-send -- [guild-id] [recipient-owner-id] [amount]` or `player-send -- [guild-vault-address] [to-address] [amount]` (`PermTokenTransfer` on the guild), stake it with `reactor-infuse` plus the `--owner-id` flag set to the guild id, or buy capacity with `agreement-open` plus the same flag.
- **Founding**: `guild-create -- [reactor-id] [endpoint] [entry-substation-id]` — 2,000,000 ualpha from your vault, see Decisions.

### UGC moderation

Structs has no global moderator — each guild sets its own name/pfp standards for member-owned objects, and the chain emits an audit event on every override. Grant moderation by rank (recommended) or per player:

```bash
# Members at rank 5 or better can moderate guild-mate UGC
structsd tx structs permission-guild-rank-set TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [guild-id] 16777216 5
# Or a single moderator on the guild object
structsd tx structs permission-grant-on-object TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [moderator-player-id] 16777216
```

Perform a moderation: `player-update-name`/`player-update-pfp`/`planet-update-name`/`substation-update-name`/`substation-update-pfp TX_FLAGS -- [target-id] "value"`. When the actor isn't the owner, the chain emits `ugc_moderated` (actor, target, field, old/new) — audit it. Note `pfpClientRenderAttributes` is **owner-only** and **not** guild-moderatable. Full philosophy + validation: [`knowledge/mechanics/ugc-moderation`](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/ugc-moderation).

### Central Bank (mint / redeem / convert)

- **Mint** tokens against Alpha collateral: `guild-bank-mint TX_FLAGS -- [alpha-amount] [token-amount]` (`--guild-id` to name a guild other than your own; raw integers; ratio captured at action time). Guild-privileged (`PermGuildTokenMint`, plus `PermTokenTransfer` on the guild vault). The Alpha collateral is taken **from the guild vault** and the minted tokens are deposited **in the guild vault** — not to the signer. Distribute with `vault-send`.
- **Redeem** tokens for Alpha: `guild-bank-redeem TX_FLAGS -- [amount]uguild.[guild-id] [min-amount-alpha]` — coin string plus Alpha slippage floor. Tokens are burned from your player vault and the Alpha arrives in your player vault. Payout is `floor(amount * collateral / supply)` but still rejected if that payout is below `min-amount-alpha`.
- **Convert** ualpha into an existing guild token at the live collateral ratio: `guild-bank-convert TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [alpha-amount] [min-amount-token]`. Debits your player vault's Alpha and credits the token to the same vault. Needs `PermTokenTransfer` on the signer. Convert-in fee stays in collateral. `min-amount-token` is the slippage floor.
- **Convert token → token**: `guild-bank-convert-token TX_FLAGS -- [amount]uguild.[source-id] [target-guild-id] [min-amount-token]` — redeems the source then converts into the target in one tx; both guilds keep their fees.
- **Confiscate & burn** (Tier 2 act of war, audited forever): `guild-bank-confiscate-and-burn TX_FLAGS -- [amount]uguild.[guild-id] [address]` — token amount first, then the address it is taken from. The destination of a `uguild.*` send must be a registered player, the structs module, or an indexed provider pool — **not IBC**.

Mint/redeem are Tier 1 within your standing-order caps, Tier 2 above. Convert is the open market path. Economics: [`knowledge/economy/guild-banking`](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/guild-banking).

## Commands reference

| Action | Command |
|--------|---------|
| Create (2,000,000 ualpha from vault, Tier 2) | `structsd tx structs guild-create TX_FLAGS -- [reactor-id] [endpoint] [entry-substation-id]` |
| Join / proxy / paid join | `structsd tx structs guild-membership-join \| guild-membership-join-proxy \| guild-membership-join-by-rank-purchase TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Rank sales (admin) / buy rank | `structsd tx structs guild-update-rank-purchase TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [base-price] [step-increase] [minimum-rank] [enabled]` / `guild-rank-purchase TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [target-rank] [max-price] [expected-rank]` |
| Treasury transfer | `structsd tx structs vault-send TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [recipient-owner-id] [amount]` |
| Invite / request (+approve/deny/revoke) | `structsd tx structs guild-membership-invite \| -request \| ...-approve \| ...-deny TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Kick | `structsd tx structs guild-membership-kick TX_FLAGS -- [player-id]` |
| Update rank / entry rank | `structsd tx structs player-update-guild-rank \| guild-update-entry-rank TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Settings | `structsd tx structs guild-update-endpoint \| -entry-substation-id \| -join-infusion-minimum \| -owner-id TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Guild UGC | `structsd tx structs guild-update-name \| guild-update-pfp TX_FLAGS -- [guild-id] [value]` |
| Moderate member/object | `structsd tx structs player-update-name \| ...-pfp \| planet-update-name \| substation-update-name \| -pfp TX_FLAGS -- [target-id] [value]` |
| Bank mint / redeem / convert / confiscate | `structsd tx structs guild-bank-mint \| guild-bank-redeem \| guild-bank-convert \| guild-bank-convert-token \| guild-bank-confiscate-and-burn TX_FLAGS -- ...` |
| Guild rank permission set/revoke | `structsd tx structs permission-guild-rank-set \| permission-guild-rank-revoke TX_FLAGS -- [object-id] [guild-id] [permission] [rank]` |

`TX_FLAGS` per [`conventions.md`](/skills/conventions.html). **Requires** [`structsd`](/skills/structsd-install/SKILL.html) on PATH and a signing key.

## Verification

- `structsd query structs guild [id]` — members, settings, owner, `rankPurchase*` fields, `joinByRankPurchaseEnabled`.
- `structsd query structs vault [guild-id]` + `structsd query bank balances [address]` — treasury.
- `guild-membership-application-all` — pending invites/requests.
- `guild-bank-collateral-address [guild-id]` — reserves.
- `guild-rank-permission-by-object-and-guild [object-id] [guild-id]` — rank-based access.

## Errors

- **Insufficient infusion** — meet `joinInfusionMinimum`, get an invite (bypasses it), or buy in if the guild sells entry.
- **is_owner** — you own a guild; transfer it before founding another.
- **Affordability on `guild_create` (`2000000ualpha`)** — the founder's **vault** holds less than 2,000,000 ualpha; fund it from your key.
- **`legacy_charter_fields_not_supported`** — the create message carried proof/nonce/consent fields; send the three-argument form only.
- **`validator_jailed`** — the named reactor's validator is jailed; pick another reactor or wait for unjail.
- **`rank_purchase_disabled` / `rank_purchase_admission_disabled` / `outside_purchase_range`** — the guild does not sell that rank (or does not sell entry); check its `rankPurchaseMinimumRank`.
- **`rank_changed` / `membership_changed` / `quoted_price_exceeded`** — your rank, guild, or the price moved since you quoted; re-read and resubmit.
- **`deletion_pending`** — the guild's entry substation is being deleted; the guild must repoint it before anyone can join.
- **under_raid** — not a guild error; see production.
- **Already member** — founding leaves your current guild if you are only a member; you cannot join twice.
- **Invite/request approve with no pending application** — membership approval requires an existing application.
- **Mint/redeem/convert failed** — insufficient Alpha/tokens, or `min-amount-token` slippage missed.
- **recipient_not_eligible** — `uguild.*` cannot go to IBC escrow or an unregistered address.
- **Permission denied / rank too low** — need PermAdmin or strictly-better rank; entry rank can't exceed your own.

## See also

- [knowledge/economy/guild-banking](https://structs.ai/knowledge/economy/guild-banking) — Central Bank, collateral, token lifecycle
- [knowledge/mechanics/permissions](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/permissions) — 25-bit values, guild rank permissions
- [knowledge/mechanics/ugc-moderation](https://structs.ai/knowledge/mechanics/ugc-moderation) — name/pfp moderation & validation
- [knowledge/lore/factions](https://structs.ai/knowledge/lore/factions) — guild politics
- [playbooks/situations/guild-war](https://structs.ai/playbooks/situations/guild-war) — coordinated conflict; [structs-permissions](/skills/structs-permissions/SKILL.html) — delegating authority
